CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left-sided lower back pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left-sided lower back pain that began after back surgery in November 2020. He underwent a microdiscectomy for a herniated disk at the L5 level that had broken off and wrapped around the spinal thecal sac, causing severe nerve pain radiating down his leg. He was treated with high-dose gabapentin postoperatively, which was difficult to discontinue. Currently, his pain is located around the area of prior surgery and is intermittent, occurring randomly and worsened by bending over. Pain is alleviated by stretching. Pain location varies day to day between left and right sides. He denies current pain radiating down his legs. He has tried ibuprofen 800 mg daily for pain management. He has not attempted icing. He reports pain when weight-bearing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain radiating down legs. Denies nerve pain. No other acute complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back surgery (microdiscectomy) November 2020

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has significant other who recommends stretching for pain relief.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient ambulatory
Back: Pain with weight-bearing. No pain with forward flexion. No pain with extension. Pain with palpation to left side around L5. No pain with palpation to right side.
Neurological: Dorsiflexion normal and intact. Patient able to push back against examiner's hands with normal strength. Normal range of motion. No pain radiating down legs.

RESULTS
X-ray of spine: No fractures. Normal spinal bone. Prior surgical site healed properly with evidence of prior intervention.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Muscle strain/pull with spinal misalignment, left lower back, status post microdiscectomy
   - Prescribed meloxicam to replace ibuprofen for improved pain management
   - Prescribed demerol for pain management
   - Prescribed physical therapy (patient established with VA physical therapy)
   - Referral to pain management for discussion of pain management strategies and consideration of non-narcotic pain management options
